name: Kentucky
overview: Kentucky does not auction property for unpaid taxes. Once the sheriff turns over unpaid tax bills, they become certificates of delinquency (liens), and each county clerk holds one sale a year where registered third-party purchasers buy those certificates by paying the amount due. It is not a bidding auction: the order in which purchasers pick certificates is set by a random drawing at the start of the sale. The Department of Revenue sets the statewide schedule; sales begin in mid-July and run into late October, and purchasers must register with the clerk at least a week ahead (and with the Department if they buy more than a few certificates). A purchased certificate earns interest of 1% per month, and the purchaser cannot take collection action until at least one year has passed.

overview_sources.quote: The sale in each county shall be administered by the county clerk.

Beginning in mid-July, county clerks offer the certificates of delinquency for sale to third party purchasers.
The selection order is determined by a random drawing at the beginning of the tax sale.

counties.how_to_bid: This is not a bidding auction: registered third-party purchasers take turns picking certificates of delinquency in an order set by a random drawing. The clerk's most recent procedures notice found (for a September 2024 sale) says the sale is conducted electronically in multiple rounds, with purchaser position set by electronic lottery, and purchasers need not be present. Purchasers register with the clerk by the stated deadline; that notice set fees of $5.00 per certificate on a priority list and $10.00 per certificate on the current list, not to exceed $250.00. Current-year procedures are not posted.

counties.how_to_bid: This is not a bidding auction: registered third-party purchasers take turns picking certificates of delinquency in an order set by a random drawing. Kenton runs an automated sale. For 2026, purchasers registered by July 6 at 4 p.m. and emailed a spreadsheet listing certificates in the order they want to purchase them. The registration fee was $10.00 per tax bill for buyers under the statutory limits (3 or fewer in Kenton, 5 or fewer statewide, under $10,000 statewide) and $250.00 above them. The county page does not describe how the order among purchasers is set.
